newsitem.title: UK: "Pocket Budget" summary issued by UK Treasury - 1.
newsitem.headline: "Pocket Budget" summary issued by UK Treasury - 1.

text.p: The following is the text of a "Pocket Budget" summary of Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's UK budget statement issued by the Treasury on Wednesday:
"THE POCKET BUDGET -- EQUIPPING BRITAIN FOR OUR LONG-TERM FUTURE"
A Budget for the many, not the few, bringing high and stable levels of growth and employment
- promoting economic stability based on low inflation and low government borrowing,
- encouraging long-term investment in technology,education and training
- modernising the welfare state to encourage work, not dependency
- providing high quality public services with more money for schools and hospitals
- moving towards a fairer tax system
- protecting the environment and health
THE CHALLENGE

Britain is full of talent and potential. We have unrivalled inventiveness and creativity. Too often this has been thrown away. We have a history of boom and bust. Low investment in education and training has left us trailing. We do not have a wide enough range of goods and services to sell. Old battles -public versus private sector and employee versus employer - have prevented progress.

The world is changing more quickly than ever before. Technology is transforming the way we work.Ever increasing trade between nations is bringing new challenges - and new opportunities. Old certainties - such as jobs for life - can no longer be taken for granted.
The challenge for business and individuals is to work together to ensure Britain can meet these challenges and everyone can play a full role.
THE OBJECTIVE

The Government's central economic objective is to achieve high and stable levels of growth and employment. In meeting this objective, the Government wants to encourage a fair society in which the many, not the few, can share in higher living standards and greater job opportunities.
THE GOVERNMENT IS COMMITTED TO REDUCING BORROWING
THE MEASURES

For many years, the British economy has not grown as fast as other industrial countries. Swings from boom to bust have made business wary of the future and investment has been lower than in other,more stable countries.
PROMOTING ECONOMIC STABILITY
A successful economy needs stability so businesses and individuals can plan ahead with confidence. Stability depends on three things:
Low inflation.

Britain has to shake off its reputation for not keeping the lid on prices. The Government has already taken action to put this right - to keep prices stable, the Government has set a low inflation target and the Bank of England is now free from political interference when setting interest rates to meet it;
Operational Independence for the Bank of England

The Chancellor has given the Bank of England responsibility for setting interest rates - the cost of borrowing money. The Government still makes the decisions on economic policy but the Bank is now free from political interference when acting to meet the inflation target set by the Chancellor.

To keep price increases down, the Chancellor has set the Bank a target of 2 per cent for underlying inflation. If inflation goes too far above or below the target, the Governor of the Bank will have to write a public letter to the Chancellor to explain why.
This new, open arrangement makes the Governments economic policy more believable -helping to maintain low inflation into the long term.
The Golden Rule

When a government borrows only to finance investment and not to fund day to day spending,it is following the Golden Rule. In other words, public spending on current goods and services and social security benefits must be met by taxes, but investment for the future can be met by borrowing.

Strict control of government borrowing. Sound public finances are essential to long-term stability. The Budget introduces new rules where the Government will borrow only to finance investment - not to fund day to day expenditure. The Government will also keep total national debt at a prudent and sensible level;
Openness. The Government is committed to building trust. It has opened its books to independent checks and, in future, plans to publish a consultation paper before each Budget.
The Budget will help bring stability to the housing market by reducing mortgage interest relief and increasing stamp duty on large property transactions.
